scope: A separate OS test process runs the production platformTaskScheduler.tick claim/start/execute/completion path and kills itself with SIGKILL while the handler is active.
Before-effect and after-effect cases share the same durable SQLite task, attempt, service identity and occurrence identity.
The after-effect case fsyncs one synthetic external effect before SIGKILL. Recovery closes the task and attempt as uncertain and never invokes the handler again.
The expired-lease state transition and empty-poll authority-loss commit are verified on SQLite and a fresh PostgreSQL 18 database.
limits: The killed process is a dedicated OS test process using the real scheduler path, not the compiled cmd/app-task-worker process making a container-backed application HTTP call.
The external effect is a test-owned fsynced file, not the exact Scheduled Digest service. It proves ambiguous-effect recovery and non-replay, not exactly-once delivery.
A stale handler cannot commit after revision/fence loss because completion checks the running state and lease again; a later compiled CLI/native backend crash drill remains useful release coverage.
